column2: The hostage is moved before you arrive.
You find a better entry point. Success.
A partner commander wants your team to support an assault on a village. Your legal advisor says the target list is shaky. What's your call?
The assault is canceled. Later, the list proves mostly wrong.
You only engage confirmed fighters. Clean operation.
The limits are ignored the moment shooting starts.
Your team has run raids five nights straight. Higher wants one more tonight. Your Marines are making mistakes. What do you do?
Approved. The next raid is flawless.
A tired mistake gets you hurt.
You lead a visit, board, search and seizure on a suspected weapons smuggling dhow at night. The crew is acting jumpy. How do you board?
Crew surrenders instantly. Rockets found in the hold.
A crewman fires from the wheelhouse.
They dump the cargo overboard while you talk.
As {rank}, you command a Raider battalion. Congress wants MARSOC cut to save money. You're asked to testify. What do you emphasize?
Budget saved. Senators praise the Raiders.
You're asked to shift Raiders from counterterrorism to great-power competition. Some old operators resist. How do you lead the change?
The force adapts. History will thank you.
You visit the family of a Raider killed under your command. His father is angry and blames you. What do you say?
He calms down. You stay in touch for years.
He doesn't want to hear it. Not yet.
A news story reveals misconduct by Raiders under your command. Your boss wants to know how you'll respond. What's your plan?
You clean house. Trust restored slowly.
More stories come out. You're relieved.
You represent US special operations at an allied summit. A foreign general proposes a joint mission with risky terms. What do you say?
The mission struggles on unclear command.
After 26 years, you're being considered for general. Your body is wrecked and your family wants you home. What do you do?
Not selected. Time to plan retirement.
You hang up the uniform with honors.
You're asked to dedicate a memorial for fallen Raiders, including some you sent into battle. What do you say?
It takes a long time. Nobody leaves.
Your battalion's injury rates are climbing and operators are burning out. Training tempo is to blame. What do you do?
Strength coaches and physical therapists work miracles.
You brief senior leaders on a sensitive operation in {country}. One asks a question you can't answer. What do you do?
Honesty is valued at this level.
Someone knows the real answer. Embarrassing.
A former Raider you served with as a captain calls you at midnight. He's out of the service and sounds like he's in crisis. What do you do?
You get him to a VA program. He's still alive years later.
He thanks you, flatly. You worry for weeks.
At a family reunion, your uncle insists Raiders are just 'Navy SEAL wannabes'. Everyone is watching. What do you do?
He doesn't listen, but your aunt is impressed.
He taps out at 12. You do 80.
He pulls a muscle. Now it's your fault.
You eat potato salad in peace.
{buddy} wants the team to pool money for a big lottery jackpot. Everyone's in. Are you?
You actually win a small share!
The team watches a military action movie. It's wildly inaccurate. {buddy} is yelling at the screen. Do you join in?
You keep a mental list of errors.
A Gold Star family organizes a memorial ruck. It's 22 miles on a weekend. Will you go?
Your feet are destroyed. Your heart is full.
The family sends a thank-you note.
A kid at a Veterans Day parade asks if you've ever been scared. What do you tell him?
His dad nods. The kid looks amazed.
He thinks you're a superhero. It's a lie.
A local gym influencer challenges you to a pull-up contest on camera. Do you accept?
You win. The video goes viral.
He wins. The video still goes viral.
RASP day one at Fort Moore. A cadre screams that half of you will quit by Friday. He's looking at you. What will you do?
You become furniture. Furniture doesn't get smoked. Mostly.
'HOOAH, SERGEANT!' He moves on, almost impressed.
He did not ask you a question. You learn that in the front-leaning rest.
A cadre demands you recite the Ranger Creed, all six stanzas, right now. You know five of them. What will you do?
The sixth stanza comes back mid-sentence. Rangers lead the way.
You blank on 'Readily will I display...' and spend an hour remembering it in the dirt.
Honesty earns pushups and an assignment to recite it 50 times tonight.
RASP 12-mile ruck, 3 hours to make it. Mile 9 and your legs are concrete. What will you do?
You cross with four minutes to spare and immediately lie in the gravel.
Your hamstring locks. You miss the time hack.
Steady was too slow by 90 seconds.
RASP combat water survival. Blindfolded, full kit, walk off the high dive. What will you do?
Splash, drop the rifle-free gear, swim out. Easy. Ish.
You panic underwater. Divers pull you out.
The cadre helps you off. With his boot.
Week three of RASP. Your shins are cracked with stress fractures. Medical offers you a recycle. What will you do?
Six weeks of healing, then you do it all again. Smarter this time.
You graduate on broken legs. Legendary, and stupid.
A shin snaps on a run. Medical drop.
RASP graduation. A Ranger places the tan beret on your head. {buddy} didn't make it. What will you do?
{buddy} says they'll be back next class. You believe it.
Big steak, bigger bar tab. Worth it.
{buddy} from a regular infantry unit says Rangers are 'just infantry with good PR.' What will you do?
You buy him a beer. Quiet confidence.
You smoke him on a 10-miler. He buys the beer.
Monday formation. Your haircut is three days old and the first sergeant says it's 'luxurious.' What will you do?
High and tight, back to standard.
You lose. You always lose this one.
Turn-in after the range. The armorer rejects your rifle for the fourth time. 'Carbon in the bolt carrier.' What will you do?
Your squad leader hands you the M240 machine gun for a 15-mile movement. Nobody else wants it. What will you do?
Your shoulders hate you. Your squad leader remembers.
Somebody left a door unlocked. The whole platoon is getting smoked. {buddy} whispers it was you. What will you do?
You own it. The smoke session ends sooner. Respect gained.
Ranger School, Darby phase. You're graded patrol leader and your squad is stumbling in the dark. What will you do?
You hit the objective on time. GO.
Ranger School, mountains of north Georgia. Freezing rain, 90 lb ruck, three hours of sleep in four days. What will you do?
You make it to Florida phase.
Your peers rank you high. That matters.
Florida phase. Waist-deep swamp at night. Something big just splashed nearby. What will you do?
It was probably a log. Probably.
It was not a log. Gator bite.
The squad bumps into you. Swearing ensues.
Day 50 of Ranger School. You see a vending machine in the woods and try to buy a soda from a tree. What will you do?
{buddy} slaps you. 'It's a tree, man.' You laugh like a maniac.
The RI writes it up for a hilarious after-action.
Ranger School peer evals. Your squad wants to 'peer' the guy who keeps falling asleep on watch. What will you do?
He gets recycled. Harsh, but he was endangering the patrol.
He stays. He thanks you. He falls asleep again.
Ranger School graduation. Your mom pins the tab on your shoulder. You've lost 30 pounds. What will you do?
Two pizzas, a cake, and a gallon of milk. Your stomach rebels.
Ranger School. You find a granola bar in an old fighting position. Eating it is a 'major minus.' What will you do?
Best granola bar of your life.
An RI sees the wrapper. Major minus.
You dream about it for weeks.
First deployment to {country}. Your first night raid. Your heart is pounding as the helicopter descends. What will you do?
You stack, flow, clear your corner. Exactly like training.
Shot through the arm on the breach.
A team leader shoves you forward. You recover. You'll be better.
Clearing a compound in {country}, you push into a room alone. A man is reaching under a mattress. What will you do?
He freezes. It was a cell phone. You did it right.
killed clearing a room in a night raid
He had a grenade. You saved the stack.
Combat jump onto an airfield in {country}. 500 feet, night, and your static line is tangled with another jumper. What will you do?
Free. Canopy opens. You hit the runway and roll.
You land hard on asphalt. Broken leg.
Reserve opens. You land off-target but alive.
killed in a combat parachute accident
Airfield seizure. Your job: clear the runway of vehicles and obstacles before the first C-17 lands in 30 minutes. What will you do?
You drive the truck off the runway. Planes land on time.
Field training at Hunter Army Airfield. The sand fleas are eating you alive. What will you do?
Your team leader nods. You're itchy for a week.
You hide the bug spray. {buddy} notices.
Joint Base Lewis-McChord. It's been raining for 40 straight days. Your gear smells like a swamp. What will you do?
Your barracks room becomes a laundromat.
Friday night in Savannah. {buddy} wants to drive back to Hunter after six beers. What will you do?
Uber home. {buddy} is mad, then thankful.
You make it back. You promise never again.
He crashes into a parked car. MPs.
You failed a PT test by 3 points and the battalion is threatening to RFS you. What will you do?
You crush the retest. Stay in batt.
You fail again. Back to regular Army.
He gets you a second chance.
You're carrying the breaching charge. The door is metal and thicker than expected. What will you do?
Door gone. So is the doorframe. Good enough.
Overpressure rattles your brain. Mild TBI.
Door holds. The team goes to a window.
Combatives tournament. You're matched against a former college wrestler. What will you do?
Rear-naked choke. He taps. The company goes wild.
He suplexes you. Your company winces.
You don't win, but you don't get tapped.
{buddy} snuck a handle of whiskey into the barracks. Alcohol is banned. Inspection is tomorrow. What will you do?
{buddy} mourns the whiskey. You both pass inspection.
JMPI before a training jump. You realize your reserve handle is rubber-banded wrong. What will you do?
Fixed. He thanks you for paying attention.
Main opens fine. Reserve not needed.
{buddy} is about to fail a land nav test and asks to follow you. It's an individual event. What will you do?
{buddy} fails. You feel bad, but it's on them.
An RI saw. Integrity violation for both.
Patrol base, 0400. You've slept 2 hours in 3 days. Your eyes close mid-sector scan. What will you do?
You wake up with nobody noticing.
Team leader finds you asleep. Article 15.
A grey-haired veteran of the 1993 Mogadishu battle speaks at your company. He asks if anyone has questions. What will you do?
He says fear never left, he just stopped listening to it. You write that down.
You listen. The room is dead silent.
{country}. Your squad is pinned by fire from a rooftop. Your team leader yells 'Suppress!' What will you do?
Your rounds keep their heads down. Squad maneuvers.
Your 40mm lands right on the rooftop. Silence.
As team leader, a private keeps failing standards. He's a good kid. The platoon sergeant asks your opinion on RFS. What will you do?
He goes to the 82nd. He'll do fine there.
He fails again. Your judgment is questioned.
You make squad leader. The previous one was beloved. Your guys keep comparing you. What will you do?
Six months later, they compare the next guy to you.
Night raid in {country}. Your team stacks on a door. You hear a woman and children inside. What will you do?
Interpreter calls them out. Women and kids exit. Clean.
A fighter used them as cover.
A child is injured in the breach.
A fighter barricaded in a room has already wounded one Ranger. What will you do?
He refuses. Now you need another plan.
Clean assault. Bronze Star with V.
Your squad finds the high-value target hiding in a spider hole. He's begging. What will you do?
The working dog attached to your squad alerts on a wall. The handler says 'something's there.' What will you do?
A fighter pops out of a hide behind you.
The Chinook carrying your squad lands hard. Smoke fills the cabin. Two Rangers aren't moving. What will you do?
Everyone out before the fire. Commendation.
Others handle the casualties. Perimeter holds.
You're a sniper team leader. A man on a rooftop is talking on a radio and watching your assault force. What will you do?
He moves off. Assault force adjusts.
He called in an RPG team.
Your Ranger medic is down and {buddy} is bleeding badly. Everyone in the regiment is trained in first responder care. What will you do?
Tourniquet, chest seal, needle decompression. {buddy} lives.
You do everything right. {buddy} doesn't make it.
The medic is only stunned. He takes over.
Twelve deployments in nine years. Your hands shake when you're not working. What will you do?
You start sleeping. Your squad notices you're calmer.
Thirteenth deployment. The shakes get worse.
You move to a training unit. The quiet is strange.
After years as a breacher, you're forgetting words and getting headaches daily. What will you do?
TBI diagnosis. Treatment helps. You're off the breach team.
Your battalion picks you and {buddy} for the Best Ranger Competition. 60 hours, nonstop events. What will you do?
You finish, but in the middle of the pack.
'I will never leave a fallen comrade.' A Ranger's body is in a building still taking fire. What will you do?
You bring him home. Silver Star.
The body is lost for 2 days.
Your squad raids a compound. Bad grid. It's a family of farmers. Everyone's terrified. What will you do?
You arrange condolence money. The family accepts.
A wounded enemy fighter lies in the courtyard. Your medic is busy. What will you do?
He lives and becomes a valuable source.
He dies. Was it your call?
Exfil helicopter is taking fire. The pilots say 60 seconds or they leave. Two guys are still clearing. What will you do?
You drag them back in 55 seconds.
One misses the bird. Second exfil required.
You catch a Ranger in your squad selling extra ammo to a civilian contact on base. What will you do?
It comes out later. You're both punished.
You keep saying 'what?' Your wife says the TV is too loud. What will you do?
You're the new platoon sergeant. Your lieutenant is fresh out of Ranger School and very confident. What will you do?
He becomes a great officer, crediting you years later.
He learns hard lessons. The platoon suffers.
Divorce papers arrive by email while you're in {country}. Your team needs you tonight. What will you do?
You do the mission. You fall apart after.
He listens. It helps a little.
Mid-firefight, a fighter steps out with hands up. {buddy} raises his weapon. What will you do?
He's taken prisoner. Laws of war upheld.
You find a laptop and cash on the objective. A teammate suggests pocketing the cash. What will you do?
Your 60mm mortar section must fire within 30 meters of friendlies. The math is tight. What will you do?
A private in your squad gets a DUI downtown. The first sergeant asks if you knew he had a problem. What will you do?
Honest answer. Lessons learned for everyone.
Your platoon is pinned. AC-130 says rounds would land 40 meters from you. What will you do?
Perfect fires. Platoon saved. Silver Star.
A grenade lands in the room with your fire team. Nowhere to throw it back. What will you do?
The grenade's fuse was partly defective. You live, badly hurt. Medal of Honor.
killed shielding teammates from a grenade
Your team survives because of you.
Your team holds a building corner while the platoon evacuates wounded. Fighters are massing. What will you do?
You hold until the last bird leaves. Distinguished Service Cross.
killed holding a corner during evacuation
Your squad leader says you need your tab to keep advancing. You've been putting it off. What will you do?
{buddy} died on the last deployment. His family asks you to speak at the funeral. What will you do?
You tell the story of {buddy} carrying you through RASP. Everyone cries.
You can't. You stand in the back.
Combat jump. Your squad lands scattered across the drop zone. Enemy fire coming from the tower. What will you do?
As first sergeant, you must decide whether to pass a soldier with a positive drug test for Ranger school. What will you do?
He fails again. Your judgment questioned.
Your first day as a Ranger platoon leader. Your platoon sergeant has 9 combat deployments; you have zero. What will you do?
He respects you for it. Partnership forms.
You smoke everyone on the run. Grudging respect.
They roll their eyes behind your back.
You get a raid tasking with 3 hours until launch. Intel is thin. What will you do?
Fast and surprising. Airfield seized in 20 minutes.
First plane takes fire on the runway.
You brief a two-star general on tonight's raid plan. He wants 'more aggression.' What will you do?
Weather is marginal for the helicopter infil. The target is only there tonight. What will you do?
The AC-130 overhead reports 'squirters' fleeing your target. Some might be civilians. What will you do?
You follow them to a second compound. Bonus target.
Ranger Orientation Program for officers. Your peers include a West Point first captain and a former college athlete. What will you do?
You all pass. Friends for life.
You have to call the parents of a private killed on your raid. What will you do?
Hardest call of your life. The father thanks you.
They wanted to hear your voice.
A private in your platoon did something heroic. Higher wants to downgrade the award. What will you do?
He gets the Silver Star he earned.
Intel says the target compound is empty of civilians. Your gut says otherwise. What will you do?
Drone spots a wedding. Raid postponed. Good call.
You take command of a Ranger rifle company. The previous commander was fired. What will you do?
You learn what went wrong. You fix it.
A female officer who earned her tab joins your company. Some NCOs are grumbling. What will you do?
Standard is standard. She earned the tab. Grumbling stops.
You're the battalion S3 (operations officer). Three missions, two helicopters. What will you do?
An American contractor is held in {country}. Your company is tasked. What will you do?
Your battalion commander rates you second of six captains. You want top block. What will you do?
Training jump at night. Winds above limits. Your men want to jump. What will you do?
A Ranger in your company is accused of misconduct on deployment. He's a star performer. What will you do?
Your company has done 40 raids in 60 days. The men are exhausted. Higher wants more. What will you do?
A documentary crew wants to film your company. PAO approves. What will you do?
Your detainees will be transferred to a partner prison known for torture. What will you do?
You're chosen to teach young lieutenants. A student is clearly struggling. What will you do?
Your company's vehicle convoy is ambushed. Lead vehicle is burning. What will you do?
You flank and destroy them. Bronze Star with V.
Major's board. Your file is good but not great. A mentor offers to call the board president. What will you do?
Your spouse says you've missed every birthday for four years. What will you do?
You take command of the 75th Ranger Regiment. Op tempo is crushing. What will you do?
You push back on some missions. Readiness rises.
A Ranger was killed by friendly fire. Higher wants to report it as enemy action. What will you do?
Family learns truth. You keep integrity.
Pentagon wants to cut the regiment's budget. What will you do?
Media wants your thoughts on Mogadishu at the anniversary. What will you do?
Three Rangers took their own lives this year. What will you do?
The Pentagon wants more Rangers. They suggest lowering RASP standards. What will you do?
Congress asks if Rangers are being over-deployed. What will you do?
The Ranger Memorial adds new names this year. You give the address. What will you do?
Twenty minutes. The silence is profound.
Your command sergeant major disagrees with your new policy publicly. What will you do?
A report surfaces of hazing in one battalion. What will you do?
After 26 years, you're offered a final command or retirement. What will you do?
Tan beret folded away. A peaceful life.
Ranger Rendezvous at Fort Moore. Old Rangers, young Rangers, beer. What will you do?
You meet a Vietnam Ranger. He buys your beer.
St. Patrick's Day in Savannah. The whole city is green and so is {buddy}. What will you do?
{buddy} makes it home. You're a hero.
A hurricane is bearing down on Hunter Army Airfield. What will you do?
Karaoke night. {buddy} dares you to perform the Ranger Creed to a power ballad. What will you do?
A third-grade class sends cards and candy. One card says 'Please don't die.' What will you do?
You tweak your back during a max deadlift. What will you do?
A kid at the airport sees your tan beret and asks if you're a superhero. What will you do?
'No, just a soldier who trains hard.' He salutes you.
You give him a scroll patch. He'll remember forever.
You're an airman at an air station waiting for an A-School slot. The swimmers there run a brutal prep workout and invite you. Do you go?
By the time your orders come, you can do the pool test in your sleep.
You overdo it and strain a shoulder.
You get fitter, but miss their tricks.
The swimmers stop inviting you. That's a bad sign.
Day one at Aviation Survival Technician A-School in Elizabeth City. The instructor says most of you won't graduate. What's your plan?
Never first, never last. You survive week one.
Instructors notice your effort and leadership.
You burn out by Thursday and instructors notice that too.
You and {buddy} quiz each other every night.
Instructors play panicked survivors in the pool. One climbs on your head and pushes you under. Your lungs burn. What do you do?
You go deep, he lets go, you get behind him. Textbook.
You swallow half the pool and get pulled out.
You muscle up for air. Not pretty.
You live to retest, but instructors remember.
During a buddy tow evolution, {buddy} cramps and goes limp for real, not as an act. Instructors haven't noticed. What do you do?
Instructors jump in immediately. He's fine. They respect the call.
You get him to the wall. He owes you forever.
You both go under. Instructors pull you out.
Week four of A-School. You can barely lift your arms. A recruiter mentions an easier rating with a signing bonus. Do you quit?
You decide you'd rather drown than quit. Dramatic, but effective.
You go to a desk job. You think about it often.
Your dad says, 'You never quit anything.' You stay.
Your family tells you to come home. It shakes you.
Half of A-School is parachute rigging and sewing. Your stitches look like a toddler made them. The instructor is unimpressed. What do you do?
Your seams get straight. You can now hem your own pants.
'Your gear keeps people alive,' the instructor says flatly.
The EMT portion of training is pure memorization. Your national registry exam is tomorrow. You're shaky on cardiac. What do you do?
You pass with room to spare.
Exhausted, you second-guess yourself. Retest needed.
The cardiac questions sink you. Retest.
You graduate A-School as an Aviation Survival Technician. Your family drove 10 hours to watch. How do you celebrate?
Your grandmother tells the waiter you're a 'lifeguard for boats'. Close enough.
Legendary night. Everyone shows up on time the next day.
Someone fights a bouncer. You're all in trouble.
Your orders arrive. You can rank your choice of air stations. What do you put first?
Bering Sea, crab boats, brutal cold. You'll learn fast.
Warm water, migrants, hurricanes. Never boring.
Quiet, until the ice rescues start.
Your first real hoist off a sailboat. The mast is swaying 15 feet each way. The flight mechanic is watching you. What do you do?
Smart. You avoid the mast and hoist the sailor from the water.
The mast catches you on the swing.
A long search pattern in rough air. You're about to vomit in the helicopter, which the crew will never let you forget. What do you do?
They notice anyway. You're 'Chum' for a month.
You lose the fight. All over your fins.
You pull a kayaker out of 45-degree water. She's shivering violently and confused. The flight back is 30 minutes. What do you do?
Wet clothes off, blankets on, handled gently. She's talking by landing.
She stops shivering. That's bad. The hospital pulls her through.
Rub her arms to warm her
Cold blood rushes to her core. Her heart rhythm goes bad.
It's 0200 on a quiet duty night. {buddy} wants to sneak out for pizza. If a case drops, you have 30 minutes to launch. What do you do?
A case drops at 0230. You're ready.
Best pizza of your life. Nobody noticed.
The alarm sounds while you're at the counter. Launch is delayed.
The delivery guy is confused by the hangar. Worth it.
A fishing boat is burning off the coast. Crew members jumped. You see three heads in the water and a fourth man still aboard. What do you do?
Three out of the water. The fourth jumps too, and you get him.
You get three. The fourth is never found.
You get him off seconds before fuel ignites.
Burns on your arms. You still get him off.
In heavy surf during a rescue, you lose a fin. The survivor is 30 yards away and drifting toward rocks. What do you do?
Slower but you reach him before the rocks.
The surf slams you both into the rocks.
The helo repositions and drops you closer. It works.
You're running late for a launch and skip part of your harness check. Your flight mech asks if you're good. What do you say?
A strap was twisted. You fix it. The mech nods.
The strap slips under load. You're dangling sideways.
You recover a teenager who drowned near a beach. It's your first body. The family is on the shore. What do you do afterward?
It helps to say it out loud.
You see his face when you close your eyes.
A training hop with a new pilot. Your hover position is drifting and you're being dragged through the water. What do you do?
Pilot adjusts. Training is for learning.
You swallow a lot of the Atlantic.
A video of your rescue goes viral. Strangers recognize you at the grocery store. {buddy} is teasing you. What do you do?
You deflect all praise. People like you more.
